observations: web-resolver-gs1: mature GS1 reference code (syntax engine, dictionary, resolver CE) plus several small community resolvers; GS1 publishes a resolver test suite on ref.gs1.org (not a repository, per prior research). Best oracle source for identifier.parse and identifier.resolve.

aas-digital-twin: most mature open source. Several independent AAS servers and SDKs (BaSyx, FAAAST, AASPX server, aas-core) and the IDTA spec repos with OpenAPI and JSON Schema. A real test tool exists (aas-test-engines, last push 2025-08) already wrapped by aas.validate.
verifiable-credentials-ssi: W3C test suites are active and give reusable vectors (JOSE/COSE, data integrity, status list). UNTP has its own test repo under GPL-3.0.
dataspace-federated: EDC connector and a DSP technology compatibility kit exist. No DPP-specific dataspace test suite was found. The Tractus-X DPP application is archived.
dlt-anchored: only small, single-maintainer or experimental repositories; none has a test suite useful for the engine.
linked-data-semantic: CIRPASS-2 ontologies and validator (JSON Schema and SHACL), LiU DPPO, OpenEPCIS DPP-Ready. SHACL shapes are the main fixture source for the interface_only data.shacl capability.
event-traceability-epcis: OpenEPCIS and FasTnT are mature; EPCIS validators and test-data generators exist, but the engine has no EPCIS check.
No official, open DPP conformance test suite was found in this search. Several vendor validators (OpenDPP, TracePass, dppvalidator) exist; treat them as comparators, not authorities.
Licence matters for reuse: GPL-3.0 (UNTP repos), AGPL-3.0 (open-dpp), BSL-1.1 (odal engine) limit copying; use these as external oracles only.
anomalies: The Zenodo API fetch ignored the keyword query and returned unrelated records, so no Zenodo software record is recorded.
The uncefact/spec-untp pushed_at value is approximate is date only, from the org listing.
GitHub topic and text searches are noisy: topic:dpp returned many unrelated projects (Discord bot library, other dpp acronyms), which I excluded.
The engine's own repository (hadijannat/dpp-conformance-engine) appeared in search results and was excluded from the inventory.
CIR4FUN java-dpp-sdk README names a CEN standard number as an alignment claim; I recorded only that the project says it is not a formal compliance implementation.
truncation: Search results capped at 200 per query (two pages of 100) and most queries have far more hits; I hand-picked about 85 repositories by relevance from roughly 820 unique search hits plus organization listings. READMEs read only up to the first 1,800 characters; test contents were not opened. Star counts and pushed_at come from the GitHub API on 2026-10-19. GitLab and Zenodo coverage is minimal: one GitLab page read, Zenodo query unusable. Further GitLab projects under opensource.unicc.org and Codeberg/Forgejo projects (CE-RISE) were not searched.
